item.title: [IGNITE-1957] .NET: Collections, dictionaries, object arrays and tuples must use handles.
item.description:
We must track handles for the following cases:

  • Collections
  • Dictionaries
  • Entries
  • Object arrays

Reason: they may have cyclic deps on other collections what will lead to infinite loops.

This change must be tested thoroughly:
1) Can we get such field which is handle?
2) Can we resolve infinite loops with collections/maps/arrays?
3) Are they referential equal after deserialization?
item.summary: .NET: Collections, dictionaries, object arrays and tuples must use handles.

status.description: The issue is considered finished, the resolution is correct. Issues which are not closed can be reopened.

comments.comment: It would be good if we fit the ticket into 1.5, but it covers pretty specific use case and it's fix will not affect backward compatibility. Hence, moving it to 1.6 with hope that we will be able to fit it into 1.5.

Pavel,

I cannot merge with master due to conflicts. One of them looks suspicious to me - something about "WriteMapEntry" handling.

Please resolve conflicts and assign back.
MapEntry handling was removed as part of IGNITE-2099: https://github.com/apache/ignite/commit/6cdd58042358049afacc10e169192a009a346846

Pavel,

My comments:
1) BinaryWriter.WriteArrayInternal - why don't you write primitive arrays as handle? But you do that for collections.
2) BinarySystemHandlers.FindWriteHandler - "supportsHandles" flag looks like a hack for me. Most types support handles, but you set "true" to only of them. This should be cleaned up.

Pavel,

Code looks good to me. Please do the following:
1) Merge with master
2) Re-run all test suites and confirm that they are green.
3) Re-assign back to me and I will merge it.

Vladimir.
